stem: A 50-year-old woman died years after a spinal cord injury. A myelin-stained section of her cord at autopsy is pale only in the medial part of both dorsal columns; the lateral and anterior white matter and the ventral horns stain normally.
oneliner: 50F + old cord injury + myelin stain pale only in medial dorsal columns, rest normal → which symptom?
ask: Which symptom did this lesion most likely cause during life?

options.A: Loss of vibration sense in both hands
options.B: Loss of vibration sense in both feet
options.D: Brisk knee jerks in both legs
options.E: Loss of pain and temperature in both feet

whyNot.A: The hands are served by the **lateral** dorsal column (cuneatus); the pale area here is **medial only**
whyNot.C: Thigh wasting needs **ventral horn** damage, and her **ventral horns stain normally**
whyNot.D: Brisk reflexes need **lateral corticospinal** damage, and the **lateral white matter is normal**
whyNot.E: Pain and temperature travel in the **anterolateral** tract, and the **anterior and lateral white matter is spared**

answer: Loss of vibration and position sense in both feet (fasciculus gracilis lesion)
why: The **medial** part of the dorsal column is the **fasciculus gracilis**, which carries vibration and position sense from the **legs**. Its loss leaves the **hands** (fasciculus cuneatus, lateral) intact.

idea.rule: The medial dorsal column carries leg proprioception and vibration; the lateral part carries arm input.
also: Fasciculus gracilis: legs (below T6); fasciculus cuneatus: arms (above T6)
Dorsal column fibers stay on the same side until the medulla
Tabes dorsalis and B12 deficiency damage the dorsal columns
Pain and temperature run in the anterolateral spinothalamic tract
